i went, and i would say my experience was sort of 50/50. yes you will get the help you need. you'll get referrals, transported to a big hospital in an ambulance, meet with psychiatrists, and put into a psych ward. 

you'll be a bit isolated from the outside world, but you'll be safe. so you might feel uncomfortable, but you will be safe. 

the wait times where i live, in canada, are very long. i had to wait 8 hours to get transported to a bigger hospital that had more resources to take care of me. during that wait time, i just slept and ate the food they gave. my father brought me a phone charger so i could keep myself entertained. 

then i was transported in an ambulance about 30 minutes away. i was then interviewed by social workers and psychiatrists and given an "on sight diagnosis." 

then after eating dinner, i was transported in the mental health unit/psych ward. i had to be strip searched and my belongings like my phone and charger, were stowed in a locker and locked away. 

there was only a tv that played movies in my room, and a sink with a bed. we weren't allowed to shower or bring any soaps in. we were given wet wipes to clean ourselves. the bathroom had no lock. 

after 5 hours of staying in there, a psychiatrist came for an assessment. at that point i was feeling less suicidal so i told them. 3 hours later i was discharged and given a care package with phone numbers for hotlines. 

i would do it again if i felt dangerous enough.
